newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU says Britain breaks beef ban, mulls legal action.
newsitem.headline: EU says Britain breaks beef ban, mulls legal action.

text.p: The European Commission is considering legal action against Britain for illegal exports of unspecified quantities of British beef to European Union and other countries, a Commission spokesman said Wednesday.

The European Union banned exports of British beef and beef products in March 1996 to protect consumer health after the British government said it was possible a human form of the fatal "mad cow" disease could be caught from eating infected beef.

In a brief statement, the EU's executive would say only that an EU inspection mission's report "confirmed suspicions" of fraudulent exports to some member states and non-EU countries. "The Commission is examining if the evident inefficiency of controls should result in infringement proceedings," it added.
Despite a barrage of questioning, the spokesman declined to give details about how much beef was exported and to which countries, saying this would hinder legal inquiries.

The announcement coincided with a hearing of British government and farmers' complaints to the European Court of Justice in Luxembourg that the Commission had overstepped its powers in imposing the worldwide ban on British beef exports.
The Court is due to issue a final ruling at the end of 1997.
